headline: GOLD ON TRACK FOR WEEKLY GAIN AS IRAN DEAL SPECULATION KEEPS DOLLAR PINNED
snippet: Gold is poised for a 2.4% weekly gain as Iran deal optimism keeps the dollar under pressure. Analysts say the historic precious metals rally could resume once 'the fog of war lifts' — gold and silver surged 66% and 135% respectively through 2025. Watch Friday's close for confirmation the bull market is intact.

headline: COPPER SMASHES $6.20/LB RECORD; CHINA'S SULFURIC ACID BAN SQUEEZES GLOBAL MINE OUTPUT
snippet: Copper futures settled at a record $6.20/lb on May 8 as China's sulfuric acid export ban — effective May through December — removes an estimated 3 million tonnes from the global seaborne market. Iran war disruptions have already tightened supply; the ban now threatens refining operations across Chile, Indonesia, and India.

headline: GOLD MINERS CRUSH THE METAL: GDX +8%, GDXJ +9% AS OPERATING LEVERAGE PLAY ROARS BACK
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) surged nearly 8% on May 6, hitting $92.67 — its highest level in over a year. The junior-focused GDXJ jumped 9% to $123.50. GDX is now up 72% over the past 52 weeks, outpacing spot gold itself. Operating leverage is kicking in as record metal prices widen miner profit margins.

headline: SSR MINING EXPLODES 20% ON BLOWOUT Q1: EPS BEATS BY 32%, $1.5B MINE SALE ON DECK
snippet: SSR Mining (SSRM) posted Q1 2026 EPS of $1.15, crushing the $0.87 consensus, as revenue surged 84% year-over-year on $4,770/oz average realized gold. Management is advancing a $1.5B cash sale of the troubled Copler mine, expected to close by year-end — a major balance sheet catalyst the market is now pricing in.

headline: SILVER47 STRIKES 38.7 g/t GOLD AND 1,713 g/t SILVER AT KENNEDY — 15km VEIN NETWORK REVEALED
snippet: Silver47 Exploration (TSX-V: AGA) reported surface rock samples up to 38.7 g/t Au and 1,713 g/t Ag at its expanded Kennedy Gold-Silver Project in Nevada. The results outline a 15km largely untested vein network across a 6,150-acre land package. No modern drilling has been conducted — CEO Galen McNamara flagged strong discovery potential at depth.

headline: MANHATTAN URANIUM (MANU) CLOSES DUAL ACQUISITIONS: 15 PAST-PRODUCING U.S. MINES IN ONE ROLLUP
snippet: Manhattan Uranium Discovery Corp. (TSX-V: MANU) completed court-approved acquisitions of Urano Energy (99.9% shareholder approval) and Pegasus Resources (98.2%). The combined company now holds 15 past-producing uranium mines across 25 U.S. properties covering 25,099 acres, creating a pure-play North American uranium platform.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM CONTRACTS HIT $90/LB — HIGHEST SINCE 2008 AS UTILITIES SCRAMBLE FOR SUPPLY
snippet: Uranium's long-term contract price has climbed to $90/lb U3O8 — the highest since 2008 — while spot holds at $86. Kazatomprom cut 2026 guidance by ~8 million lbs. Utilities' uncovered requirements are at record levels, with Cameco's president warning: 'The wall of demand between now and 2045 cannot be avoided.' AI data center reactor deals are accelerating procurement.

headline: CHILE LITHIUM EXPORTS SURGE 175% IN APRIL — SQM-CODELCO PARTNERSHIP SIGNALS MARKET RECOVERY
snippet: Chile's lithium carbonate exports hit $498M in April 2026 — a 175.6% year-over-year surge — as the SQM-Codelco partnership ramps output. China spot prices have recovered to CNY 24,920/t, up 137% year-over-year. Q1 lithium carbonate revenue reached $1.108B (+147.7% YoY), confirming the post-2024 crash recovery is accelerating.

headline: THE HORMUZ REOPENING TRADE WALL STREET FORGOT: WHY MINERS COULD BE THE STEALTH PLAY
snippet: If a U.S.-Iran peace deal reopens the Strait of Hormuz, energy traders win — but junior gold and silver miners, now priced against 'crisis gold,' could actually surge further as geopolitical risk premium reprices into operating margins. Benzinga walks through the asymmetric case for mining stocks in a ceasefire scenario.

headline: GOLD, SILVER, AND MINERS AT 'NEW LEVELS OF ABSURD' — AND THE SETUP STILL LOOKS CONSTRUCTIVE
snippet: FXStreet's May 8 technical review finds gold, silver, and miners breaking through price levels analysts called 'absurd' just months ago — and the structure remains constructive. Near-term consolidation is possible as Iran deal speculation adds noise, but the medium-term setup still favors higher prices for leveraged mining exposure.
